_limits: A record here is evidence THE RECORD EXISTS with that title, abstract, full text or registry content. It is NOT evidence of efficacy, safety, a therapeutic window, clinical readiness, or that any delivery gate has moved, for any agent named, in EMC or in any other disease.

TOLERATED IS NOT ENGAGED. Every safety and pharmacokinetic figure recorded here describes what the source reported about administration and plasma exposure. None of it is evidence that an oligonucleotide reached, entered or silenced a target inside a solid tumour. The memo keeps those two classes of evidence in separate sections for exactly this reason.

The Journal of Clinical Oncology 2014 article (NCT00938574) is NOT open access (Europe PMC isOpenAccess=N, no PMCID) and its body was not retrieved. Questions only the body can answer are recorded as UNKNOWN in the memo, not inferred.

A ClinicalTrials.gov search returning a small totalCount is a CONVENIENCE SAMPLE of that registry under that query spelling, not a census of oligonucleotide trials in solid tumours. It says nothing about EU CTIS, jRCT, ChiCTR or any other national register.

The Silence Therapeutics press releases recorded here are COMPANY STATEMENTS retrieved verbatim from the company's own site. Retrieval makes the quotation reliable; it does not make the claim inside it a measurement.

publications.title: First-in-human phase I study of the liposomal RNA interference therapeutic Atu027 in patients with advanced solid tumors.
publications.authors: Schultheis B, Strumberg D, Santel A, Vank C, Gebhardt F, Keil O, Lange C, Giese K, Kaufmann J, Khan M, Drevs J.
publications.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
publications.abstract_verbatim: Purpose: Atu027 is a novel liposomal RNA interference therapeutic that includes a short-interfering RNA (siRNA), which silences expression of protein kinase N3 in the vascular endothelium. Atu027 has previously been shown to inhibit local tumor invasion as well as lymph node and pulmonary metastasis in mouse cancer models. This first-in-human study aimed to assess the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of Atu027 while evaluating therapeutic effects on both primary tumors and metastatic lesions. Patients and methods: Thirty-four patients with advanced solid tumors received 10 escalating doses of Atu027 without premedication, as one single followed by eight intravenous infusions twice per week during a 28-day cycle. Response was monitored by computed tomography/magnetic resonance imaging at baseline, at the end of treatment (EoT), and at final follow-up (EoS), and was assessed according to RECIST. Results: Atu027 was well tolerated up to dose levels of 0.336 mg/kg; most adverse events (AEs) were low-grade toxicities (grade 1 or 2). No maximum tolerated dose was reached. Plasma levels of siRNA strands and lipids were dose proportional, peaking during 4-hour infusion. Disease stabilization was achieved in 41% of patients at EoT (n = 14 of 34 treated patients); eight patients had stable disease at EoS, and some experienced complete or partial regression of metastases. sFLT1 (soluble variant of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1) decreased from pretreatment levels in most patients after dose levels 04 to 10. Conclusion: Atu027 was safe in patients with advanced solid tumors, with 41% of patients having stable disease for at least 8 weeks. In view of these results, further clinical trials have been initiated, and sFLT1 will be investigated as a potential biomarker.
publications.⛔ what_the_abstract_does_not_contain: No mention of a tumour biopsy, biodistribution, tissue sampling, PKN3 measurement in any tissue, or any pharmacodynamic readout other than the PLASMA protein sFLT1. The word 'tumor' appears only as a disease descriptor and in the RECIST imaging context.

what_was_measured_verbatim.pharmacokinetics: A total of 11 subjects was included in the PK analysis—the 3 subjects from the lead-in safety period, 4 from Arm 1 and 4 from Arm 2. ... T max for all compounds was achieved at or just after the end of infusion (4 h). The mean t 1/2 was ~10 h for Atu027 siRNA, ~20 h for AtuFect01 and ~17 h for DPyPE. The C max and AUC of Atu027 siRNA remained relatively constant over the consecutive administrations with both once- (Arm 1) and twice-weekly (Arm 2) administration (~150 ng/mL for C max and ~1000 h·ng/mL for AUC).
what_was_measured_verbatim.biomarkers: Of the 301 analytes assessed as potential biomarkers, 46 and 59 analytes changed significantly from baseline in Arms 1 and 2, respectively, and 13 biomarkers were significantly associated with response status. Once adjusted using the Benjamini–Hochberg method for multiple hypothesis testing, only one analyte (Factor VII in Arm 1) changed significantly from baseline, and one (Angiopoietin-2) was significantly associated with response status at the first follow-up.
what_was_measured_verbatim.safety: Four subjects (17%) reported Grade 4 AEs ( n = 1 increased lipase level, n = 1 hyperglycemia, n = 2 decreased neutrophil count). A total of 23 SAEs was reported by 16 subjects. Only two SAEs were judged to be related to treatment—one Grade 3 SAE of pneumonia in Arm 1 was judged to be possibly related to both Atu027 and gemcitabine, and one Grade 2 SAE of fever in Arm 2 was judged to be possibly related to gemcitabine (both recovered).
what_was_measured_verbatim.atu027_related_ae: Twice as many AEs were judged to be related to gemcitabine ( n = 110) as to Atu027 ( n = 49). Consistent with the phase 1 study, the most frequent Atu027-related AE was fatigue; however, this was never dose-limiting.
what_was_measured_verbatim.survival_as_reported: median PFS Kaplan–Meier estimates 5.33 (95%CI 1.51–6.02) months Arm 2 versus 1.81 (95%CI 0.39–5.49) months Arm 1, p = 0.3985, 22% censored; post-hoc metastatic-only mPFS 1.61 (95%CI 0.39–2.07) Arm 1 versus 2.89 (95%CI 1.02–7.26) Arm 2, p = 0.0247, 21% censored; mOS 5.6 Arm 1 versus 7.8 Arm 2, p = 0.6082, 35% censored; post-hoc metastatic-only mOS 3.3 Arm 1 versus 6.7 Arm 2, p = 0.5943, 26% censored.
what_was_measured_verbatim.authors_own_conclusion_on_the_target: Our clinical results support the significant involvement of the vascular endothelium in the spread of cancer, and thus the further investigation of its target role.

publications.title: Evidence of RNAi in humans from systemically administered siRNA via targeted nanoparticles.
publications.authors: Davis ME, Zuckerman JE, Choi CH, Seligson D, Tolcher A, Alabi CA, Yen Y, Heidel JD, Ribas A.
publications.full_text_route: Europe PMC fullTextXML for PMC2855406, HTTP 200, 64930 characters
publications.agent: CALAA-01 — a cyclodextrin-polymer nanoparticle carrying an siRNA against RRM2, surface-decorated with PEG and a human transferrin targeting ligand. NOT a GalNAc conjugate and NOT hepatocyte-directed.
publications.administration: intravenous, days 1, 3, 8 and 10 of a 21-day cycle, 30-minute infusion
tissue_evidence_verbatim: In order to ascertain whether the targeted delivery system can provide effective delivery of functional siRNA to human tumors, we investigated biopsies from three patients from three different dosing cohorts; patients A, B and C, all of whom had metastatic melanoma and received doses of CALAA-01 of 18, 24 and 30 mg-siRNA/m 2 , respectively.

Given the highly experimental nature of this protocol, the regulatory process at both the local and federal levels explicitly precluded a provision for mandatory biopsies in all patients. Therefore, biopsies were obtained on a voluntary basis.

Samples A, B and C1, analyzed in a blinded fashion, demonstrated a heterogeneous distribution of nanoparticles only in post-dosing tumor tissue. The nanoparticles can localize intracellularly in tumor tissue and are not found in the adjacent epidermis.

Samples C1 post and C2 post reveal the highest number and intensity of stained regions, B post exhibits a decreased amount of staining relative to samples C1 post and C2 post, A post does not reveal the presence of the stain, and all the pre-dosing samples are completely negative for the stain. This is the first example of a dose-dependent accumulation of targeted nanoparticles in tumors of humans from systemic injections for nanoparticles of any type.

Significant reduction in RRM2 is observed (mean scoring of RRM2 from the 10 sections was reduced 5-fold) after treatment while TfR levels are somewhat elevated (mean scoring of TfR from the 10 sections was increased 1.2-fold) in the C1 pre and C1 post samples.
the PCR data from the C2 pre vs. C2 post samples (collected 10 days apart) provide direct evidence for RRM2 mRNA reduction via the treatment of the patient with the nanoparticles
⛔ limits_stated_by_the_authors_themselve: Since samples A pre and B pre are from tissues collected many months before the initiation of siRNA treatment, the fraction of the overall reduction in mRNA observed in A post and B post attributable to the nanoparticle treatment cannot be directly ascertained.
Unfortunately, we were not able to perform PCR on the C1 samples.

The IHC data from patient A do not reveal changes in RRM2 expression after dosing, while results from patient B are indicative of reductions in maximal RRM2 expression (IHC scoring of the regions of maximal expression showed a 1.5-fold decrease) but the overall mean expression levels remained relatively constant.
In these biopsies TEM images were dominated by melanosomes inhibiting the identification of the nanoparticles (data not shown).
publications.⚠ scale: Three patients, one tumour type (metastatic melanoma), cutaneous/subcutaneous lesions accessible to voluntary biopsy. The RNAi-specific cleavage-fragment result comes from ONE patient at the highest dose. The trial itself is TERMINATED with no registry results record.

gate_verdict.question_it_asks: is there a validated way to deliver an oligonucleotide to a non-hepatic solid tumour
gate_verdict.atu027_reason: Both trials measured administration tolerability and PLASMA pharmacokinetics. Neither prespecified a tumour biopsy, a biodistribution measurement or any tissue-level PKN3 readout, and the open-access full text of the later trial contains zero occurrences of biopsy, biodistribution, knockdown, tumour tissue, pharmacodynamics or immunohistochemistry. A drug that was given systemically and tolerated is not a drug shown to have engaged a target inside a solid tumour.
gate_verdict.⚠ additional_reason_specific_to_this_age: Atu027's intended target cell is the VASCULAR ENDOTHELIUM, by the sponsor's and the authors' own description. Endothelium lines the lumen and is on the blood side of the vessel wall. Even a fully successful Atu027 would therefore not have demonstrated that an oligonucleotide crosses the vasculature into a tumour parenchyma — which is what an EWSR1::NR4A3 fusion-junction ASO would have to do in an EMC nodule.
gate_verdict.⭐ what_did_land_on_the_gate: PMC2855406 / PMID 20305636 — a systemically infused, non-GalNAc, non-hepatic-targeted siRNA nanoparticle found intracellularly in melanoma tumour biopsies in a dose-correlated way, with reduced target mRNA and protein versus pre-dosing tissue and an RNAi-specific cleavage fragment in one patient. Three patients, one accessible tumour type, voluntary biopsies, two of three baselines archived months earlier, and the trial TERMINATED. It is a proof of principle at n=3 from 2010, not a validated delivery route, and it is nothing at all about EMC or its myxoid matrix.
gate_verdict.⛔ this_memo_does_not_regrade_anything: No route is unparked, no blocker is re-graded, and research/method-watch.md is untouched. This is evidence plus a recommendation.

unknowns: Whether the Journal of Clinical Oncology 2014 article (NCT00938574) reports any tissue-level measurement in its body. It is not open access, no PMCID exists, and its full text was not retrieved. The registry outcome list contains no tissue endpoint and the abstract names only the plasma protein sFLT1, but a paper's abstract and its registry record are a floor on what it measured, not a ceiling — CALAA-01 is the counter-example in this very memo.
What the Int J Clin Pharmacol Ther 2012 record contains. Europe PMC carries no abstract for it and it is not open access.
Whether the correct Atu027 dose in NCT01808638 is 0.235 or 0.253 mg/kg. The paper states both.
Why the ClinicalTrials.gov actual enrolment for NCT01808638 (29) differs from the publication's 3 lead-in plus 23 treated.
What the NCT01808638 prespecified 'circulating microRNA' biomarker endpoint showed. The primary publication reports 301 plasma analytes and never mentions microRNA.

Whether the Atu027 programme was formally discontinued, and on what stated reason. No such statement was retrieved; the last sponsor statement located (2016-04-05) announced partnering plus further pre-clinical delivery work, not a stop.

What the EPHARNA (NCT01591356) prespecified tumour-biopsy EphA2 modulation and apoptosis endpoints showed. The 2025 conference abstract reports only safety and RECIST. hasResults is false. This is the single most gate-relevant open question surfaced here.
Whether any of the systemic-ASO trials listed above reported tumour-tissue target engagement. Only their registry existence and status were read.
recommendation: Do NOT unpark RT-ASO and do NOT re-grade BLK-DELIVERY on Atu027. Nothing in either trial is a tumour target-engagement result.

Raise with whoever owns systems/graph/blockers.json that BLK-DELIVERY's evidence base now has a named human precedent it did not have (PMC2855406) and a named ONGOING trial with the right endpoint prespecified (NCT01591356). Neither clears the blocker; both change what 'no precedent exists' may honestly be taken to mean.
Chase the EPHARNA tissue endpoint. It is the only live, registered, on-gate readout located, at an academic centre, with pre/post core biopsies prespecified, and it is a $0 watch rather than a spend.
Do not put any of this in the fusion-junction ASO manuscript as a delivery claim. A 2010 n=3 melanoma result and an unreported endpoint in an ongoing trial are not a delivery route for an EMC nodule.
